prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for everyone — the best firm for you depends on your exact location in Miami, budget, roof type, and whether you need help with insurance claims or HOA approvals. Instead of one name, here’s a practical way to find and pick the best hurricane-rated roofer in Miami, plus what to require from them.

What to require / check
- Miami‑Dade product approvals (Notice of Acceptance, NOA) for the materials and system they propose. Hurricane-rated systems must be installed per the NOA.
- Manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred) — these matter for warranties.
- Florida contractor license and local registrations; proof of general liability and workers’ comp insurance.
- Written, itemized estimate that lists materials, brand/models, wind‑rating (mph), flashing details, fastener types (ring‑shank nails, stainless or hot‑dip galvanized), and the specific NOA numbers.
- Written warranties: manufacturer warranty and a workmanship/installation warranty (get length and transferability in writing).
- Permits and inspections: contractor must pull required permits and provide final inspection/CO if applicable.
- Experience with hurricane straps, uplift-resistant attachments, and local code (Florida Building Code / Miami‑Dade requirements).

Questions to ask every contractor
- Do you have experience with Miami‑Dade NOA installations? Can you show NOA sheets for materials you’ll use?
- Are you manufacturer‑certified for this product? Can you provide certificate?
- How do you fasten tiles/shingles/metal to meet the required uplift rating?
- Who is my point of contact? How do you handle change orders?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and photos of completed hurricane‑rated roofs?
- What is your payment schedule? (Avoid large upfront cash payments.)

Red flags
- No proof of insurance or license, no permits, or unwillingness to provide NOA/manufacturer paperwork.
- Very low bid with vague scope or “we’ll use whatever materials are cheapest.”
- High-pressure sales (demanding immediate signatures) or asking for full payment up front.

Types of contractors to consider
- Reputable local Miami roofing firms that demonstrate strong hurricane experience and NOA installations.
- National firms with a local presence that are certified by major manufacturers.
- Specialty shops for the roof type you want (metal, concrete tile, TPO/modified bitumen, etc.).

How to pick
- Get at least 3 written bids and compare them line‑by‑line, not just price.
- Favor contractors who show the NOA installation method and include it in the scope.
- Check online reviews (Google, Yelp), the Better Business Bureau, and confirm references.
- Verify contractor’s license number with Florida’s DBPR and check complaint history.

If you want, I can:
- Prepare a short checklist/email you can send to contractors requesting bids.
- Provide a shortlist of well‑rated local roofers — tell me your Miami zip code and whether you prefer tile, metal, or shingle and whether you need insurance-claim help.

Which material is best for hurricanes?
- Properly installed standing seam metal and properly fastened concrete/flat tile systems are commonly preferred for high-wind areas (when installed per NOA).
- Architectural shingles can be used if they and the installation meet the applicable wind ratings and NOA.

If you give your zip code and your roof type (tile/metal/shingle/flat), I’ll draft the checklist you can send to contractors and help narrow options to highly qualified firms in your area.
